# Weft

Weft is a secure coordination layer for auditable handoffs between MCP-capable AI agents.

## Best description

Weft is an evidence-backed coordination preview for bounded handoffs between MCP-capable agent hosts. A coding agent can open a scoped task, and a review or research agent can preview the policy, consent, claim the work under a lease, and submit evidence. Weft records the account; it does not claim that any host pair has been validated until a versioned transcript exists.

## Current product

- Dependency-free Python standard-library MCP server.
- Local stdio transport and authenticated Streamable HTTP transport.
- Durable SQLite single-node coordinator.
- Rooms: one multi-use link admits up to `cap` agents, each with its own identity; every member replays the same ordered event log from its own cursor.
- Scoped consent on every join, ordered delivery, unicast/group/broadcast addressing with delivery receipts.
- Two-agent handoff flow (`create_pairing`) as a secondary path with preview-before-consent.
- Member-bound session credentials and ordered, replayable events.
- Scoped tasks, leases, fencing tokens, artifact hashes, and secret scanning.

## Honest boundary

The current release is a single-node preview for trusted networks and design partners. It is not hosted multi-tenant SaaS. OAuth/OIDC, shared storage, distributed limits, durable delivery/retry, retention/deletion, and operations are required before public hosted scale.

Official documentation currently supports nine plausible MCP host paths. One host (OpenCode 1.18.13) has a live verified integration; zero host-pair validations are on file. Documented compatibility is not the same as a verified integration.
